thread.title: Tech Today: Chips' Tariff Risk, Spotify a Must-Own, Tesla Passes the Hat

author: Barron's
title: Tech Today: Chips' Tariff Risk, Spotify a Must-Own, Tesla Passes the Hat
text:
Here are some things going on today in the world of tech :
Chips' Tariff Risk Shares of several semiconductor names are taking it on the chin this morning, after Morgan Stanley's Joseph Moore warned that the Trump administration 's tariff moves increase risks to the group, particularly the analog chip names.
In the report, titled "tariffs could turn yellow flag into red," Moore writes that "at this stage of the cycle, we think the potential of further semi stock outperformance is limited as multiples remain capped and earnings upside is more measured in contrast to significant beats/raises we saw last year.
"On the other hand, even the slightest whiff on the demand front could lead to significant decline in stocks."
Moore advises picking "companies with more defensive characteristics like high margins and free cash flow," such as Analog Devices ( ADI ), versus "companies with more commodity exposure and lower margins" such as Cypress Semiconductor ( CY ).
He also likes TE Connectivity ( TEL ) and Amphenol ( APH ).
It appears this bit of news is not sitting well with several semi stocks. For example, shares of Micron Technology ( MU ), though not a focus of Moore's report, are down $1.86, or 3.4%, to $53.16.
Shares of Nvidia (NVDA) and Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) are also lower, though Intel (INTC) is up.
Adjusting for Google's Slap Alphabet (GOOGL) is set to report earnings results this afternoon , after the closing bell.
As I indicated on Friday , the expectations have generally been favorable for Alphabet along with its mega-cap brethren Facebook (FB) and Amazon.com (AMZN), which report on Wednesday and Thursday, respectively.
The Street is, on average, modeling $25.58 billion in revenue and $9.66 per share in GAAP net income.
However, the biggest news heading into the quarter was of course the European Union 's imposition of a nearly $5 billion fine last week for what it said were abuses by Alphabet's Google unit of its Android mobile software's dominance of the market. And Alphabet filed a form 8-K with the Securities & Exchange Commission saying it is going to incur that fine this quarter.
And so that means adjusting those consensus estimates, writes Credit Suisse 's Stephen Ju , who this morning reiterates an Outperform rating on Alphabet stock, and cuts down his own earnings-per-share estimate for $9.74 to $2.56.
He's still bullish on Google's improvements in its keyword search business as far as monetization, and the growing contribution of the non-search businesses such as YouTube , and cloud computing. Ju maintains a $1,330 price target on Alphabet.
Alphabet stock today is up $5.31, or 0.4%, to $1,203.19.
Tesla's Asking Everyone to Help Shares of Tesla (TSLA) are down $11.97, or almost 4%, at $301.61, following a report yesterday by The Wall Street Journal 's Tim Higgins stating that the company has "asked some suppliers to refund a portion of what he electric-car company has spent previously," citing a Tesla memo sent to a supplier.
Higgins notes that Tesla in the memo calls the refunds "an investment" in Tesla, and points out that "all suppliers were being asked to help it become profitable."
Cheers for II-VI Shares of fiber-optic component maker II-VI (IIVI) are down 20 cents to $43.65, despite an upbeat assessment this morning from Paul Silverstein with Cowen & Co ., who initiated coverage of the stock with an Outperform rating and a $57 price target, writing that the company has a "leadership position" in a "diverse number of long-tailed, high-growth markets," of which two of the most interesting are " silicon carbide ," a material increasingly going into electric vehicles , and 3-D sensing , the market for optical components that helps make possible things such as Apple 's (AAPL) " Face ID " function.
Silicon Carbide, or "SiC," is going to be "the most significant opportunity for IIVI over the next five years measured by growth and profitability," Silverstein believes.
"We estimate IIVI's SiC revenue will increase by over 300% to over $150M or ~10% of FY20 revenue from under $40M or less than 5% of FY17 revenue, driven by strong IIVI solutions together with robust applications growth."
As for 3-D, "we project 3D-Sensing revenue will increase to over $130M or 8% of FY20 revenue from de minimis levels in FY17," and the profit margin is above 50%, he notes: "this represents highly profitable growth."
Remember that 3-D sensing is the market that fell apart on Friday because of a warning from WIN Semiconductor ( 3105TW ). If Silverstein's concerned about that, he doesn't indicate it in his note.
Spotify Is a Must-Own Shares of Spotify (SPOT) are up $3.03, or 1.7%, to $185.82, after BTIG 's Richard Greenfield this morning started the stock with a Buy rating, and a $230 price target, writing that it is a " must-own stock ."
Greenfield confesses he had been "waiting for a better entry point" in the stock, because he's been fascinated by the story since meeting Daniel Ek , its chief executive and chairman, back in 2007.
The strategy of waiting isn't working, so he's decided to jump aboard as "the Spotify platform is simply too powerful/valuable to wait any longer to embrace SPOT."
"We believe Spotify will be a long-term winner in a category that remains in its infancy (meaning subscription music)," writes Greenfield.
The company is more "focused" and has more "singularity of purpose" than competitors such as Apple and Amazon and Google, he argues.
It is "the dominant brand name in subscription music worldwide," with the exception of China.
He sees the company spreading beyond just music, into things such as podcasts .
"While it remains early days, with Spotify's podcast catalog far smaller than Apple and others and a podcast experience that clearly needs to improve and make non-music content more visible, we believe Spotify's users very much want access to a robust array of non-music content."
